newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM demands united front against crime.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM demands united front against crime.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday Russians must form a united front to fight rising crime, Interfax news agency said.
"The main question today is can the authorities curb the rise of crime in vitally important areas of society," Chernomyrdin said in a speech to interior ministry officials.
"For this we must consolidate the healthy forces in society in the search for a way out of the crime crisis and create a united front to resist the rise in crime."

Corruption is rife and violent crime has risen sharply since communist rule ended in 1991, with mafia-style gangs emerging and gangland killings becoming common. Victims include businessmen, politicians and media figures.
Chernomyrdin said police and other security services had prevented the "total criminalisation of Russian society" but ordinary Russians did not feel safe.
"Crime today is a factor which really poses a threat to state security," he told a meeting at which Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov was due to outline the ministry's plans for 1997.
"None of the other problems facing our country can be ranked with the problem of crime."
Chernomyrdin said that 20 percent to 50 percent of Russia's economy was now unofficial or illegal.
He called for a system to be worked out to tighten checks on movement of capital, property transactions and investments in businesses.
Chernomyrdin called for parliament to speed up work in passing a new criminal code. He also promised to try to pay all wage debts owed to ministry employees by the end of the year.
